proof_summary: Take \(n=1408\) and exhaust all \(1\le k<1408\): after computing \(\phi(1408-k)/2\), almost every resulting number is shown composite by an explicit proper divisor, while exceptional cases are eliminated by a base-2 Fermat congruence failure or direct evaluation of the tiny endpoint values. Thus none of the 1407 possible choices of \(k\) yields a prime.
